chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has an illness and cannot lie down, and ablution is difficult for him while he is sitting leaning on pillows; sometimes he dozes off while in that state. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He performs ablution.' I said to him: 'Indeed, ablution is difficult for him due to his condition.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the sound becomes faint for him, then ablution becomes obligatory upon him.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'He delays Dhuhr and prays it with Asr, combining the two, and similarly Maghrib and Isha.'
ai.seo_question: What are the prayer and ablution rules for someone who cannot lie down due to illness?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the specific threshold for ablution validity in cases of severe illness, establishing that the loss of auditory awareness (khufiyat al-sawt) triggers the obligation to renew wudu, rather than mere sleep. It further integrates the principle of ease (taysir) by permitting the combination of prayers (jam' taqdim), reflecting the Shia juristic approach to accommodating physical hardship without compromising ritual integrity. This ruling is foundational in Usul al-Fiqh for determining the precise moment of 'loss of presence' in prolonged states of weakness.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moammar Bin Khallad who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about a man with an illness, not be able upon the lying down, and the Ablution (Wudhu) is difficult upon him, and he sits leaning with the pillow. So sometimes he dozes off and he is seated upon that state. Heasws said: ‘When the sounds are concealed from him, the Ablution (Wudhu) is Obligated upon him’. And heasws said: ‘He can delay Al-Zohr (Salaat) and pray with along with Al-Asr, gathering between the two, and similar to that is Al-Magrib and Al-Isha’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who suffers from a certain illness because of which he is not able to lie down. It is difficult for him to take Wudu’ in a sitting position and leaning against something. He may also slumber when he is sitting. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must take Wudu’.’ I then said, ‘Taking Wudu’ is difficult for him with such condition.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘When he cannot hear any sound Wudu’ becomes necessary on him.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible for him to delay al-Dhuhr Salah (prayer) to perform it along with al-‘Asr Salah (prayer) and al-Maghrib Salah (prayer) with al-‘Isha’ Salah (prayer).”’
